blockers: Phase 1a promoted Backgrounds and Merits/Flaws, and Phase 1b promoted Graces, Bedlam, and the 19 Grace-Forging/Assumption-type Charms (118 of 279 total); noble/common creation-track enforcement, Major/Minor Grace-count enforcement, the remaining Glamour Charms (including forging-the-heart-grace's own real prerequisite, Shape-Forged Servant), Pox/Affliction/Blight Charms, Behemoth-Forging Charms, Glamour Sorcery, Wyld Artifacts, and Adjurations are all still unimplemented, and Exalted1eEditor.tsx has no isFairFolk branch or dedicated Powers-section UI exposing the new Charm catalog to end users (matching Alchemical's own still-deferred Charms-browsing UI precedent).
Rules, guided-creator, migration, and browser test suites have not been run for this family yet.

'fair-folk' is a legal stored sheetType (added when this project's five-family schema foundation was first scaffolded, before any per-family promotion phase) but is still absent from definition.tsx's user-facing variants list -- no new Fair Folk character can be created through the UI yet, though an already-existing Fair-Folk-typed record remains editable via the shared ExaltedFamilyStatePanel.tsx exactly as every other locked family's blank familyState placeholder is.
notes: Exalted: The Fair Folk supplied and reviewed cover to cover. 263 core-book rows reviewed and inventoried under docs/references/exalted1e/fair-folk/inventory/: the character-creation overview (split into separate common- and noble-raksha rows), the four base castes (Diplomat/Entertainer/Warrior/Worker), the twelve named noble hybrid castes, the five Graces (Cup/Ring/Staff/Sword/Heart) with their forging rules, the Bedlam mechanic (the raksha's Limit-Trait analog) including all four Virtue-specific Curses, the five new Backgrounds (Birth/Freehold/Gossamer/Retinue/Style), the altered Backgrounds (Artifact/Familiar/Manse/Backing-Contacts-Influence) and the excluded ones (Followers/Resources), the core signature mechanics (Wyld-damage immunity, Craft (Glamour), Wyld Stunts/Bonuses, Gossamer-and-Glamour, Mutation, Shaping Actions/Reality Shaping, Shaping Combat basics, Oaths, Cold-Wrought Iron), all of Chapter Five: Raksha Magic end to end (all five per-Grace Charm trees, the universal Assumption-type Charm tree, the Vexing/Questing rules, Glamour Sorcery/Wyld Artifacts/Adjurations/Behemoths, and the narrowly-scoped sixth shinma Nirupadhika), and a triage pass across the remaining Chapters One/Two/Six/Seven that found and added the two remaining genuinely player-facing items (the Gossamer Manta vehicle and the post-creation Experience and Training Time table) and definitively confirmed, via an exhaustive book-wide text search, that Fair Folk has no dedicated Merits/Flaws section anywhere in the book. That universal gap is now filled by a second source book, the Exalted Players Guide's Chapter One, 'Merits and Flaws' -- 73 more rows (37 merits + 36 flaws, 336 total), derived from Lunar's already-verified transcription of that chapter's full 88 pg-merit-*/pg-flaw-* rows rather than an independent re-read, since the chapter is explicitly universal across all five planned families. 15 of the 88 were skipped as inapplicable to a raksha -- a being of pure Wyld/chaos that is not Exalted at all, with no Essence-reincarnation cycle, no anima or Caste Mark, no blood lineage, and no access to core Exalted Sorcery (e.g. the Dragon-Blooded-only Legendary Breeding, the Celestial-Exalted-only Known Anathema/Permanent Caste Mark/Greater Curse/Throwback, the Abyssals-and-Ghosts-only Death-Taint, the Lunars-only Chimera/Limited Forms, and the Exalted-only Sworn Brotherhood/Beacon of Power); several included rows were reinterpreted for the raksha's own framework (Large Size/Small reframed around Assumption-type shapeshifting Charms instead of Lunar forms, Cache/Debt reframed around the Gossamer Background instead of Resources, Vice/Callous cross-referenced to Bedlam instead of the Great Curse, and Mutation/Weak Essence flagged as unusually strong fits since raksha are Wyld-stuff given shape starting at Essence 2), each judgment call flagged verbatim in that row's own notes. **Exalted: The Fair Folk is now reviewed cover to cover, including the universal Merits/Flaws gap.** A later pass added two small sets of universal (non-splat-restricted) artifact catalog rows, bringing the total to 351: 6 rows derived from Lunar's already-verified transcription of the Exalted Storyteller's Companion's universal 'Further Wonders' artifact catalog (Ghost Cestus, Sling Bow of Ice, The Golden Viper, Land Ship, Singing Staff, Eye of Autochthon -- a fifth source book for this family), and 9 rows freshly transcribed from a sixth source book, Savage Seas, whose 'Artifacts of the Waves' section is likewise a universal naval-artifact catalog (Cargo Preservation Spindles, Armor of Aquatic Puissance, Steelsilk Sails, Storm Sapphire, Cord of Winds, Wavecleaver Daiklaive, Light Implosion Bow, Lightning Ballista, and a reference-only Artifact Ship Weapons summary table). The Light Implosion Bow's own text explicitly names Fair Folk as capable users; the Lightning Ballista carries one flagged judgment call over whether its 'unExalted' phrasing bars a raksha who nonetheless manipulates Essence. Nothing promoted to a production catalog yet. Chapter Six's Mountain Folk (a wholly separate playable-adjacent race with its own extensive character creation) was deliberately not inventoried here -- out of Fair Folk (raksha) scope. Locked pending schema/rules/creator/editor implementation and passing tests across all five planned families. A final cross-splat supplement-triage pass added 14 rows (351 -> 365) from Exalted: Blood and Salt: a Lintha-connection Character Backgrounds reinterpretation sidebar, a Bluehaven approach-navigation rule, four regional Character Concepts lists, seven new Artifacts (including the Talisman of the Cult of Dukantha, which grants Infernal sorcery access), one new Hearthstone (Jewel of Stability), three mundane equipment items; the rest of the book's NPC/monster stat-block material was reviewed and confirmed out of scope, and four reprinted artifacts (plus, where applicable, a reprinted Hearthstone and two reprinted/superseded spells) received citation notes on their existing rows rather than new duplicate rows. promotableEntries (279) is a preliminary keyword-based estimate of rows meant to become a strict catalog entry (Graces, Circle Spells, Oaths, Merits/Flaws, Backgrounds), matching Abyssal's approach in verification.ts. This has not been verified against a real built catalog and likely undercounts, since this pass's keyword heuristic missed Fair Folk's own Circle Spell and Oath naming conventions on a first look (they were folded back into the promotable side once found) -- treat as approximate until Fair Folk's own schema/catalog phase recomputes it precisely. Phase 1a (Backgrounds plus Merits/Flaws catalog promotion) mirrors Lunar/Abyssal/Sidereal/Alchemical's own starting phase exactly. 'fair-folk' was already a legal, schema-validated stored sheetType (added when this project's five-family schema foundation was first scaffolded, before any per-family promotion phase); this phase did not need to add it. `fairFolkBackgrounds` in definitions.ts (13 ids) resolves the inventory's own determination: five wholly new ids (Birth, Freehold, Gossamer, Retinue, Style, from Chapter Four's 'New Backgrounds' section); six altered shared ids kept with raksha-specific mechanics (Artifact, Familiar, Manse, Backing, Contacts, Influence -- the last three explicitly described as rare but not excluded, scoped only to standing among mortals in Creation); and two unaltered shared ids, Allies and Mentor, INCLUDED rather than held back, since the Common Raksha Character Creation summary affirmatively names 'a dot of Allies, Contacts or Mentor' as a real option a commoner's zero free Background dots make hard-won -- the same kind of textual confirmation Lunar's own Background section relies on, unlike Alchemical's silence-based exclusion of the same three ids. Followers and Resources are excluded outright per the source's own 'Raksha do not use these Backgrounds' instruction. `backgroundIdsBySheetType['fair-folk']` in schema.ts now resolves to this real 13-entry set (was an empty placeholder). For Merits/Flaws, `dragonblooded-merits-flaws.ts`'s `appliesTo` enum was widened to include `'fair-folk'`, added to 75 shared catalog entries (73 inventoried `pg-merit-*`/`pg-flaw-*` rows resolving one-for-one, except the two dual merit/flaw split pairs -- `mutation-merit`/`mutation-flaw` and `favor-merit`/`favor-flaw` -- each counted twice at the catalog-entry level); a new `fairFolkOnlyTraits` export mirrors `alchemicalOnlyTraits`. No new Fair-Folk-only entries or `sharedCostOverrides` were needed -- every applicable row keeps its underlying shared cost unchanged, confirmed directly for Destiny (the source's 'Destiny and Exaltation' sidebar caps only Celestial/Abyssal/Infernal Exaltation, a process raksha never undergo, so Destiny correctly falls through to the uncapped 1-5 shared range). Several included rows required reinterpretation for a raksha's own non-Exalted framework, each judgment call documented verbatim in that row's own `notes` field in the Fair Folk inventory rather than duplicated into the shared catalog file (matching Alchemical's own precedent): Large Size/Small keyed to the universal Assumption-type shapeshifting Charm tree instead of Lunar forms; Cache/Debt keyed to the Gossamer Background's own documented 'effective Resources' dot table instead of the excluded Resources Background; Vice/Callous cross-referenced to Bedlam (this splat's Limit-Trait analog) instead of the Great Curse; Unskilled's floor reframed around Caste Abilities instead of Favored Abilities; Prodigy included by analogy to Dragon-Blooded/Sidereal (whose Caste/Favored Ability structure closely parallels a raksha's own) despite being excluded for Solar/Abyssal/Lunar by name and for Alchemical by a separate, Attribute-favoring rationale; Destiny/Dark Fate/Unbidden Oracle included as selectable despite a flagged Loom-of-Fate conceptual tension, since raksha are canonically native to the Wyld outside Creation's Loom of Fate and the source text itself states no eligibility restriction; and Mutation/Weak Essence flagged as unusually strong, barely-adapted fits, since raksha are literally Wyld-stuff given shape and every raksha starts at Essence 2 exactly as Weak Essence's own 'other magical beings' clause requires. `promotedEntries` grew from 0 to 88 (13 Backgrounds + 75 Merits/Flaws); `checksum` stays empty, matching Alchemical's own Phase 1a precedent exactly -- neither Backgrounds (which live in `definitions.ts`) nor Merits/Flaws (a subset of the shared `dragonblooded-merits-flaws.json`) live in a `fair-folk-`-prefixed catalog file this project's `scripts/audit-exalted-sources.mjs` glob would hash; checksum will only become non-empty once a future phase adds a real `fair-folk-*.json` catalog file (e.g. Charms or Graces). Fair Folk's Charms/spells remain correctly rejected via the existing placeholder branches in schema.ts's `powers.spells`/`charmIdsBySheetType` (out of scope this phase). Correction to prior phases' framing: `Exalted1eEditor.tsx`'s shared `ExaltedFamilyStatePanel.tsx` component already renders a basic Fair Folk Graces/Active-Assumption/Feeding-Notes/Oaths panel unconditionally for any Fair-Folk-typed character record (the implicit final branch of that component's sheetType switch, predating this phase) -- 'unreachable through the character-creation UI' is and was only ever true for *creating* a brand-new Fair Folk record via `definition.tsx`'s `variants` list, never for *editing* one that already exists, exactly the same nuance already corrected for Alchemical. Full verification battery run: typecheck, lint, format check, the full unit+integration suite (including the new 48-test `exalted1e-fair-folk.test.ts` and the extended `dragonblooded-merits-flaws-catalog.test.ts`), `scripts/audit-exalted-sources.mjs` (0 issues), the Exalted e2e smoke specs, and a production build. Fair Folk remains locked exactly as before: `certifiedAt` stays null, and Phase 6's all-five-families-together rule still prohibits adding Fair Folk to `definition.tsx`'s `variants` list on its own. PHASE 1B (Graces, Bedlam, Grace-Forging/Assumption Charms): promoted 30 more entries (88 -> 118) across three new `fair-folk-`-prefixed catalog files. `fair-folk-graces.json` (6 rows: `graces-overview` plus one row each for Cup/Ring/Staff/Sword/Heart) transcribes each Grace's full rating table verbatim; a new `fairFolkGraces` export in `definitions.ts` documents the four Virtue Graces' feeding mapping (Cup<-Compassion, Ring<-Temperance, Staff<-Conviction, Sword<-Valor; Heart has no feeding Virtue and its rating is status-fixed, not freely raised with bonus points). `fair-folk-bedlam.json` (5 rows: `bedlam-overview` plus one row per Virtue-specific Curse) required splitting the inventory's own single compound `virtue-bedlam-curses` row into four real per-Virtue inventory rows (`curse-of-hubris`/`curse-of-namelessness`/`curse-of-alienation`/`curse-of-meekness`, all still citing p. 113/PDF 114) before promotion, mirroring Lunar's own `the-great-curse`/`curse-of-the-*` inventory-level split precedent exactly -- no new mechanics text was invented, only the original's own per-Virtue paragraph breaks used as the split points, and every inventory row that cross-referenced the old compound id was rewired to the new split ids (generically to all four for Bedlam-overview-level references, specifically to the one matching curse for Grace-level references). That rewiring surfaced an important, independently cross-verified finding: the Curse a broken Grace inflicts does NOT match that Grace's own feeding Virtue --  breaking Cup inflicts the Curse of Alienation (Temperance's Curse, not Compassion's), breaking Ring inflicts the Curse of Meekness (Valor's, not Temperance's), breaking Staff inflicts the Curse of Hubris (Compassion's, not Conviction's), and breaking Sword inflicts the Curse of Namelessness (Conviction's, not Valor's) -- confirmed from both the Curses' own row text and each `forging-the-(grace)-grace` Charm's own cross-reference text independently. `fair-folk-charms.json` (19 rows) promotes two real, page-cited, Zod-validated Charm trees: 'Grace Forging' (11 entries -- the six 'Forging the (Grace) Grace' Charms including the exotic sixth Way/shinma-Nirupadhika Grace, plus five parallel Freehold-anchor Charms -- Arcane Redoubt, Stronghold, Glory, Fountainhead, Throne Room) and 'Assumption' (8 entries -- the universal, Grace-independent gateway Charms rooted in shinma Nirakara that let a raksha exist as a shaped creature at all). `forging-the-heart-grace`'s own real prerequisite, Shape-Forged Servant, falls outside this phase's 19-entry scope, so it is kept honestly in `prerequisiteText` and a `reviewFlags` note rather than fabricated into `prerequisiteCharms` (which, mirroring Alchemical's own `superRefine` enforcement, requires every id to resolve within the same catalog). Every Charm also carries a `comboRules` field (mirroring the field every other Exalted family's Charm schema requires): all 19 default to Combo-eligible with no restrictions, since this phase's own source review found no explicit per-Charm Combo-restriction sentence in any of their transcribed text -- an honest reflection of what was found, not an assumption that no such restriction exists anywhere in the book. In `schema.ts`, `familyState`'s fair-folk branch now restricts `graces` keys to the five real Grace ids (was an unrestricted string-keyed record) and adds a `bedlamVirtueId` field (nullable Virtue id) tracking only the resulting *state* of which Curse, if any, is currently active -- Bedlam's own channel-counting trigger mechanic is explicitly session/scene-tracked play-table bookkeeping this app cannot observe, matching the established precedent (Alchemical's Clarity gain/loss triggers) of leaving such mechanics unmodeled. `charmIdsBySheetType['fair-folk']` now resolves to the real 19-entry set (was an empty placeholder); spells remain correctly rejected (no Glamour Sorcery catalog exists yet). A new `fromVersion < 13` migration cleans any stray non-Grace keys out of an existing character's `graces` record and backfills `bedlamVirtueId: null`, mirroring Sidereal's/Lunar's/Alchemical's own prior field-addition migration precedents exactly; `EXALTED1E_SCHEMA_VERSION` bumped 12 -> 13. A new `FairFolkGracesPanel.tsx` component (mirroring `LunarShapechangingPanel.tsx`'s structure) renders a Bedlam Virtue selector bound to the new `bedlamVirtueId` field plus collapsible reference entries for all five Graces and all four Curses, wired into `ExaltedFamilyStatePanel.tsx` alongside its existing bare Graces-dots/Active-Assumption/Feeding-Notes/Oaths panel -- still reachable only by *editing* an already-existing Fair-Folk-typed record, not by *creating* one, exactly as Phase 1a's own correction already established. No dedicated Charms-browsing UI branch was added to `Exalted1eEditor.tsx`'s shared `ExaltedPowersSection`, matching Alchemical's own identical, already-accepted precedent of deferring that UI even after its own Charms catalog was promoted. `checksum` is no longer empty (cb18dfb4), now that `fair-folk-*.json` catalog files exist for `scripts/audit-exalted-sources.mjs`'s glob to hash; the Bedlam inventory split also required rewiring every affected row's `crossReferences` array, re-verified with zero audit issues afterward. Full verification battery run: typecheck, lint, format check, the full unit+integration suite (including the new 13-test `fair-folk-charms-catalog.test.ts` the extended 87-test `exalted1e-fair-folk.test.ts` (including Phase 1b's own `fromVersion < 13` migration coverage), and a new 5-test `tests/integration/fair-folk-graces-panel.test.tsx` exercising the new panel directly), `scripts/audit-exalted-sources.mjs` (0 issues), the Exalted e2e smoke specs, and a production build. Fair Folk remains locked exactly as before: `certifiedAt` stays null, and Phase 6's all-five-families-together rule still prohibits adding Fair Folk to `definition.tsx`'s `variants` list on its own.
